title: Session journal
description: C8 (draft): records of the engine's session journal (ADR-0014). A session key names its newest session; a session holds its system prompt, its route alias, its messages in order, live and archived by compaction, and the steps of its turns; an `InboxDelivery` per inbox event C6 `inject` accepted is kept beside the sessions and never removed (ADR-0037 section 3); a `Mark` forgets one message and is never removed (ADR-0051 section 5). A `PruneRearm` per session holds the wait of its last proactive prune (ADR-0098). C4G shapes are free-form objects in their canonical C4G serialization, not restated here.

Session.description: One conversation. The session with the highest `id` of a key is its current one.

id.description: Session id, unique in the journal.

key.description: Session key, the `--session` name; also sent as the C4G `session_key`.

system_prompt.description: The system prompt the session's first turn built and every later turn sends unchanged. Absent until that turn; an absent or empty prompt is built again by the next turn.

route.description: Route alias C6 `set_route` stored, on which the session's turns run; absent means the engine's default route (the `DefaultRoute`, else the configured one). A new session of the key starts without one.

Message.description: One message of a session. The session's live set, the messages a turn sends, is its messages with `active` true in `seq` order.

seq.description: Position in the session, from 0 without gaps over live and archived messages. A compaction keeps the `seq` of the messages it archives and numbers its compacted set after the highest one.

turn.description: Turn that appended the message, from 1. A compacted set carries the session's last turn.

message.description: A C4G `Message`, stored as its canonical C4G serialization.

active.description: Whether the message is in the session's live set; absent means true. An archived message keeps its content.

compacted.description: Whether a compaction archived the message; absent means false. `active` false with `compacted` true: replaced by a compacted set; `active` false with `compacted` false: taken back by a rewind, which the engine does not produce.

n.description: Insertion position of the message over the whole journal, from 1, unique. The engine writes it on every message; a 0.6.0 journal's messages are numbered in `(session, seq)` order.

at.description: Unix time in seconds the engine wrote the message; absent on messages a 0.6.0 journal held.

origin.description: `turn` for a message a turn appended (the user prompt, the assistant's messages, tool results), `compaction` for a message of a compacted set. The engine writes it on every message; a 0.6.0 journal's message is `compaction` when its bytes equal those of an archived message of its session with a lower `seq` or the compressor's summary recognizer (ADR-0025) accepts it, else `turn`.

Step.description: One step of a turn: a request sent to the gateway and what its last attempt reported.

request_id.description: C4G `request_id` of the step, `s<session>-t<turn>-<step>-<tag>`, the tag 12 lowercase hex digits drawn at random for each run of the turn; steps of a 0.5.0 journal have no tag.

route.description: A C4G `RouteInfo`: the last `route` event of the step.

usage.description: A C4G `Usage`: the last `usage` event of the step.

InboxDelivery.description: The engine's durable record of one inbox event C6 `inject` accepted: the highest accepted attempt, the turn it started and that turn's delivery once the channel reported it. One record per event, kept across restarts and never removed.

attempt.description: The highest accepted C6 `InjectRequest.attempt` of the event.

turn.description: C6 `TurnId` of the turn that attempt started.

delivery.description: C6 `Delivery` the channel reported for the turn with `report_delivery`; absent until then.

Mark.description: A forget mark on one message. The message is left out of every history search while one of its marks has no `lifted_at`. A mark through a session names each message the session held when it was made, one mark per message. Marks are never removed, so each keeps the time, reason and command of its mark and of its lift.

id.description: Mark id, unique in the journal.

at.description: Unix time in seconds the mark was made.

reason.description: Why the owner asked to forget the message.

provenance.description: The owner's command that made the mark: `s<session>-t<turn>-n<n>`, the turn that ran it and the `n` of that turn's prompt. `-n<n>` is absent until that turn is journaled.

lifted_at.description: Unix time in seconds the mark was lifted; absent while it is live.

lifted_provenance.description: The owner's command that lifted the mark, in the form of `provenance`; absent while it is live.

DefaultRoute.description: The engine's default route alias a global C6 `set_route` stored, at most one per journal: a session that stores no route runs on it instead of the configured `engine.default_route`, across new sessions and restarts. Absent means the configured one.

PruneRearm.description: The rough tokens a session's live set must reach before the next proactive prune of old tool results (ADR-0098), at most one per session: the last kept prune's rough tokens after it plus the most of the tokens it reclaimed, the trigger and the minimum reclaim. A compaction of the session removes it; absent means no wait.

tokens.description: Rough tokens of the live set the next proactive prune waits for.
